Planning Django App

The planning package contains the Django app that powers the network planning dashboard. It wires together ReactPy components, database-backed device catalogues, and the server-driven routing layer exposed at /.

High-level responsibilities

  • Serve the ReactPy dashboard via planning.views.dashboard_view().

  • Provide simple JSON endpoints (e.g. /add_device/) for catalogue updates.

  • Persist available device models with planning.models.DeviceModel.

  • Relay simulator updates to connected clients via Channels consumers.

  • Surface admin tooling and signal hooks for catalogue change notifications.

Data model

DeviceModel encapsulates reusable device catalogue entries. Fields include:

Field

Description

category

Logical grouping (e.g. Router, Switch, Server).

type

Device type used by ReactPy when seeding UI defaults.

model

Vendor/model identifier or internal SKU.

ports

Number of default interfaces exposed in the dashboard.

display

Human-readable label shown in the catalogue.

created_at

Timestamp automatically managed by Django.

updated_at

Timestamp automatically managed by Django.

View layer

  • planning.views.dashboard_view() mounts the ReactPy dashboard and ensures catalogue seeding on first run.

  • planning.views.add_device() provides a lightweight JSON endpoint for creating new catalogue entries (used by the ReactPy admin component).

Real-time integration

planning.consumers exposes Channels consumers that broadcast catalogue changes. Paired with the reactpy_components._notifier helper they ensure the ReactPy catalogue updates across browser sessions without a full page refresh.

Signals

planning.signals listens for planning.models.DeviceModel saves and deletions. Whenever a catalogue record changes, the signal emits a notification that wakes the in-process ReactPy dashboard and any subscribed Channels listeners.

Testing

Unit tests live in planning.tests and cover view responses, model behaviour, and regression scenarios for the simulator integration points. Use python manage.py test planning during development.

Signal handlers for planning app.

We implement lightweight post_save/post_delete handlers for DeviceModel that: - send a Channels group message so any websocket consumer can react - attempt to call an in-process notifier (if present) so ReactPy components - subscribed to that notifier reload immediately in a single-process dev server

This file intentionally tolerates absence of Channels or the notifier so it won’t crash in minimal environments.
